Docker CVE-2026-34040 Lets Attackers Bypass Authorization and Gain Host Access Apr 07, 2026 Vulnerability / DevSecOps A high-severity security vulnerability has been disclosed in Docker Engine that could permit an attacker to bypass authorization plugins ( AuthZ ) under specific circumstances. The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-34040 (CVSS score: 8.8), stems from an incomplete fix for CVE-2024-41110 , a maximum-severity vulnerability in the same component that came to light in July 2024. "Using a specially-crafted API request, an attacker could make the Docker daemon forward the request to an authorization plugin without the body," Docker Engine maintainers said in an advisory released late last month. "The authorization plugin may allow a request which it would have otherwise denied if the body had been forwarded to it." "Anyone who depends on authorization plugins that introspect the request body to make access control decisions is potentially impacted."
